On this page

A minimal example ​

Five helmets on a plaza, made from two files: a converted glTF model, and a small hand-written scene that imports it and places it five times. The model is never copied. The scene only says where it goes.

The two files ​

FileMade byHolds
helmet.tsrmosaic gltf-pack from DamagedHelmet.glbThe model: 27 nodes for its buffer, bufferViews, accessors, images, textures, material and mesh. About 3.5 MB
helmet-plaza.tsrmosaic pack from helmet-plaza.mosaic.jsonThe scene: six nodes and five transforms, a little over 1 KB. It imports helmet.tsr

Each is a zip holding an index.json and one .ndjson table per component type:

helmet.tsr                              helmet-plaza.tsr
├─ index.json                           ├─ index.json        (imports helmet.tsr)
├─ khronos::gltf::buffer.ndjson         └─ core::transform.ndjson
├─ khronos::gltf::bufferView.ndjson
├─ khronos::gltf::accessor.ndjson
├─ khronos::gltf::meshPrimitive.ndjson
├─ khronos::gltf::material.ndjson
├─ khronos::gltf::texture.ndjson
├─ khronos::gltf::image.ndjson
├─ khronos::gltf::sampler.ndjson
└─ core::transform.ndjson

The scene ​

The plaza is a small tree of nodes. Each one has a core::name, most have a core::transform, and core::child links hold the tree together:

Near row ─┐                       ┌─ Left plinth  ──▶ helmet
          ├─▶ Pair ───────────────┤
Far row  ─┘                       └─ Right plinth ──▶ helmet
Spinner  ────────────────────────────────────────────▶ helmet
  • Left plinth and Right plinth each place the helmet, 1.5 m either side of the middle.
  • Pair holds both plinths. It has no transform of its own.
  • Near row and Far row each hold the same Pair, 2 m in front and 2 m behind, so the pair and everything under it appear twice. That's four helmets.
  • Spinner places a fifth helmet on its own: raised, turned a quarter turn and scaled to 60%.

The arrow to the helmet crosses files. d6c1d2ba-… is the id of the helmet's mesh node insidehelmet.tsr. That works because helmet.tsr was converted with --stable-ids, so its ids are the same every time it is rebuilt.

The index on each core::transform reference is a line number in core::transform.ndjson, counting from 0. The core::name and core::child references have no index: everything they say is in their id.

Building it ​

bash
# 1. the model, with ids that stay the same every time it is converted
mosaic gltf-pack DamagedHelmet.glb helmet.tsr --stable-ids

# 2. the scene, from its source document
mosaic pack helmet-plaza.mosaic.json            # -> helmet-plaza.tsr

# 3. one renderable file, following the import
mosaic compose helmet-plaza.tsr                 # -> helmet-plaza.glb

The source document, helmet-plaza.mosaic.json, is the scene as one readable file: the index with the component rows beside it, and schemas referenced by path. mosaic pack turns it into the archive: it writes the rows as core::transform.ndjson and inlines the schema. See Packing a dataset.

What composing does ​

mosaic compose reads helmet-plaza.tsr, follows its import to helmet.tsr, and layers the helmet underneath the scene. Then it walks the core::child links from the roots (Near row, Far row and Spinner) and writes a glTF node for every placement it reaches. The result has five helmets in it, but the mesh, the images and the 3.7 MB buffer are each written once and shared by all five.

Nothing about the helmet was restated in the scene. If the model is converted again, or improved, the plaza picks up the change the next time it is composed. See Composing a GLB.
